name: Norse Greenland
native: Eystribyggð and Vestribyggð (the Eastern and Western Settlements)

ledger.x: c. 986: Erik the Red founds the Eastern Settlement at Brattahlíð. G1: 'The Landnámabók reports that in 982 he sailed west' and settlement began after 986 CE; the founding fleet was 25 ships, of which 14 reached Greenland. 986 is the page's lower bound, not a date it gives; G2 has the Norse presence beginning in the…
1261: the Greenland colony accepts the Norwegian king.

c. 1350: the Western Settlement is empty. G2: 'The Western Settlement was abandoned around 1350.' G1: in 1350 Ívar Bárðarson sailed there and found no one living; the 1355 expedition under Paul Knutsson found no Norse; G1 allows an abandonment anywhere in 1350-1400.
1408: the last written record of the Norse in Greenland.

certainty.note: Settlement districts along the fjords with no frontiers; the inland ice and the Eastern/Middle/Western boundaries are approximate.
